To draw the orthographic projections of line $AB$:

1. **Given Data:**
   * Length of line $AB = 50\text{ mm}$ (True Length).
   * Point $A$ is $10\text{ mm}$ above HP and $20\text{ mm}$ in front of VP.
   * Line is inclined to HP by $65^	ext{o}$ and parallel to VP.
2. **Front View (FV):**
   * Locate front view of point $A$ ($a'$) $10\text{ mm}$ above the $XY$ reference line.
   * From $a'$, draw the front view $a'b'$ of length $50\text{ mm}$ inclined at $65^	ext{o}$ to the $XY$ line, since the line is parallel to VP and its inclination to HP is seen in the front view.
3. **Top View (TV):**
   * Locate top view of point $A$ ($a$) $20\text{ mm}$ below the $XY$ line (on the projector from $a'$).
   * Since the line is parallel to VP, its top view will be parallel to the $XY$ line. Project point $b'$ down to the projector line drawn from the locus of $a$ to get top view $ab$, which lies horizontally parallel to $XY$ with a length equal to the plan length ($50 \times \cos(65^	ext{o})$).
proTip: When a line is parallel to one plane, its projection on that plane shows the true length and true inclination.
